## Purpose and Scope

This document covers LightLLM's Prefill/Decode (PD) separation feature, which allows splitting the prefill and decode phases of inference across separate nodes or processes. This architecture enables optimized resource utilization by dedicating different hardware configurations to prefill (compute-intensive) and decode (memory-intensive) operations.

For information about standard single-node deployment, see [Standard Deployment](#7.1). For multi-node tensor parallelism without PD separation, see [Multi-Node Setup](#7.4).

## Architecture Overview

The PD separation system consists of three main components: prefill nodes that handle initial token processing, decode nodes that handle iterative token generation, and a PD master that coordinates requests between them.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Client Layer"
        Client[Client] --> PDMaster[PD Master]
    end
    
    subgraph "PD Master Node"
        PDMaster --> HttpServerManager["HttpServerManager"]
        HttpServerManager --> RouterManager["RouterManager"]
        RouterManager --> PrefillScheduler["Prefill Request Scheduler"]
        RouterManager --> DecodeScheduler["Decode Request Scheduler"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Prefill Node"
        PrefillScheduler --> PrefillRPC["PDPrefillInferRpcServer"]
        PrefillRPC --> PrefillBackend["ChunckedPrefillForPrefillNode"]
        PrefillBackend --> PrefillModel["Model Inference"]
        PrefillKVManager["PrefillKVMoveManager"] --> PrefillTransObj["KVTransConnectObj"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Decode Node"
        DecodeScheduler --> DecodeRPC["PDDecodeInferRpcServer"]
        DecodeRPC --> DecodeBackend["ContinuesBatchBackendForDecodeNode"]
        DecodeBackend --> DecodeModel["Model Inference"]
        DecodeKVManager["DecodeKVMoveManager"] --> DecodeTransObj["KVTransConnectObj"]
    end
    
    subgraph "KV Transfer"
        PrefillTransObj <--> KVTransfer["NCCL P2P Transfer"]
        KVTransfer <--> DecodeTransObj
    end
    
    PrefillBackend --> PrefillKVManager
    DecodeBackend --> DecodeKVManager
```

**System Component Mapping**
- PD Master: Uses `pd_master_start()` function and standard HTTP/Router components
- Prefill Node: Uses `ChunckedPrefillForPrefillNode` backend with `PrefillKVMoveManager`
- Decode Node: Uses `ContinuesBatchBackendForDecodeNode` backend with `DecodeKVMoveManager`
- KV Transfer: Implemented via `PyNcclCommunicator` with P2P communication

Sources: [lightllm/server/api_start.py:330-391](), [lightllm/server/router/model_infer/mode_backend/continues_batch/pd_mode/prefill_node_impl/prefill_kv_move_manager.py:31-248](), [lightllm/server/router/model_infer/mode_backend/continues_batch/pd_mode/decode_node_impl/decode_kv_move_manager.py:34-390]()

## Run Modes and Configuration

The PD separation system operates in six distinct run modes, each serving a specific role in the distributed inference pipeline.

| Run Mode | Purpose | Key Backend Class | Configuration Parameters |
|----------|---------|-------------------|-------------------------|
| `normal` | Standard single-node inference | `ChunkedPrefillBackend` | Standard parameters |
| `pd_master` | Request coordination and scheduling | HTTP/Router only (no inference) | `--pd_master_ip`, `--pd_master_port` |
| `prefill` | Initial token processing and KV generation | `ChunckedPrefillForPrefillNode` or `DPChunkedForPrefillNode` (with DP) | `--pd_master_ip`, `--pd_master_port` |
| `decode` | Iterative token generation | `DecodeNode` or `DPForDecodeNode` (with DP) | `--pd_decode_rpyc_port` |
| `nixl_prefill` | NIXL-optimized prefill with chunked transfer | `NIXLChunckedPrefillForPrefillNode` or `NIXLDPChunkedForPrefillNode` | `--nixl_pd_kv_page_num`, `--nixl_pd_kv_page_size` |
| `nixl_decode` | NIXL-optimized decode with coordinated loading | `NIXLDecodeNode` or `NIXLDPForDecodeNode` | Same as decode mode |
| `config_server` | Multi-master node discovery | HTTP server for PD master registry | `--config_server_host`, `--config_server_port` |

### Backend Selection Logic

The `ModelRpcServer.init_model()` method selects the appropriate backend based on run mode and configuration:

```python
# From model_rpc.py
if is_prefill_node:
    if self.args.dp > 1:
        self.backend = DPChunkedForPrefillNode(self.info_queue, self.mem_queue)
    else:
        self.backend = ChunckedPrefillForPrefillNode(self.info_queue, self.mem_queue)
elif is_nixl_prefill_node:
    if self.args.dp > 1:
        self.backend = NIXLDPChunkedForPrefillNode(self.info_queue, self.mem_queue)
    else:
        self.backend = NIXLChunckedPrefillForPrefillNode(self.info_queue, self.mem_queue)
elif is_decode_node:
    if self.args.dp > 1:
        self.backend = DPForDecodeNode(self.info_queue, self.mem_queue)
    else:
        self.backend = DecodeNode(self.info_queue, self.mem_queue)
```

### Key Configuration Parameters

```python
# From api_cli.py
--run_mode: ["normal", "prefill", "decode", "nixl_prefill", "nixl_decode", "pd_master", "config_server"]
--pd_master_ip: IP address of PD master node (default: "0.0.0.0")
--pd_master_port: Port for PD master communication (default: 1212)
--pd_decode_rpyc_port: RPyC port for decode node KV manager (default: 42000)
--select_p_d_node_strategy: ["random", "round_robin", "adaptive_load"]
--config_server_host: Config server host for node discovery
--config_server_port: Config server port for node discovery
--nixl_pd_kv_page_num: NIXL mode KV page count (default: 16)
--nixl_pd_kv_page_size: NIXL mode KV page size (default: 1024)
```

### Run Mode Detection

The system detects PD mode at multiple layers:

```python
# In HttpServerManager
self.pd_mode: NodeRole = NodeRole(self.args.run_mode)
assert self.pd_mode in [NodeRole.P, NodeRole.D, NodeRole.NORMAL, NodeRole.NP, NodeRole.ND]

# In RouterManager
self.is_pd_run_mode = self.args.run_mode in ["prefill", "decode", "nixl_prefill", "nixl_decode"]
self.is_pd_decode_mode = self.args.run_mode in ["decode", "nixl_decode"]

# Automatic scheduling adjustments
if args.run_mode == "decode":
    args.router_max_wait_tokens = 0  # Minimize decode latency
```

Sources: [lightllm/server/api_cli.py:7-77](), [lightllm/server/router/model_infer/model_rpc.py:123-150](), [lightllm/server/httpserver/manager.py:105-106](), [lightllm/server/router/manager.py:95-96](), [lightllm/server/api_start.py:266-269]()

## Prefill Node Implementation

The prefill node handles the initial processing of input tokens and generates KV cache data that must be transferred to decode nodes for subsequent token generation.

### Process Architecture

**Prefill Node Component Interactions**

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Main Process"
        RouterManager["RouterManager"] --> ModelRpcClient["ModelRpcClient"]
        ModelRpcClient -->|RPC via Events| ModelRpcServer["ModelRpcServer"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Inference Process"
        ModelRpcServer --> Backend["ChunckedPrefillForPrefillNode<br/>or DPChunkedForPrefillNode"]
        Backend --> Model["TpPartBaseModel.forward()"]
        Backend -->|Put KVMoveTask| InfoQueue["mp.Queue (info_queue)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "KV Move Manager Process"
        InfoQueue -->|Get KVMoveTask| KVMoveManager["PrefillKVMoveManager"]
        KVMoveManager --> TransLoop["task_dispatcher_loop()"]
        TransLoop -->|Manage| TransConnects["Dict[decode_node_id,<br/>KVTransConnectObj]"]
        TransConnects -->|Create| TransProcess["KVTransProcess"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Transfer Process (per GPU)"
        TransProcess --> NCCLInit["PyNcclCommunicator.init()"]
        NCCLInit --> P2PGroup["NCCL P2P Group"]
        P2PGroup -->|send()| DecodeNode["Decode Node"]
        TransProcess -->|Access| MemQueue["mem_queue[device_id]"]
    end
    
    Model -->|Write| MemManager["MemoryManager.kv_buffer"]
    MemManager -.->|Shared| MemQueue
```

### Key Components

**Backend Classes:**
- **`ChunckedPrefillForPrefillNode`**: Single DP prefill backend with `_router_filter_get_can_run_reqs()` and `_alloc_kv_move_task()`
- **`DPChunkedForPrefillNode`**: Multi-DP prefill backend with load balancing across DP instances

**KV Transfer Management:**
- **`PrefillKVMoveManager`**: Main coordinator process started by `start_prefill_kv_move_manager_process()`
  - Maintains `self.trans_connect_objs: Dict[int, KVTransConnectObj]` for active connections
  - Runs `task_dispatcher_loop()` to process KV transfer tasks from `info_queue`
  - Implements connection cleanup with `check_and_clean_dead_trans_connect_objs()`

- **`KVTransConnectObj`**: Per-decode-node connection manager
  - Connects to decode node via `DecodeKVMoveRpycClient` on `pd_decode_rpyc_port`
  - Manages task queue and transfer processes per GPU
  - Implements health checking with `is_connect_ok()`

- **`KVTransProcess`**: NCCL transfer worker (one per GPU)
  - Initializes NCCL with `_init_nccl()` using allowed port range
  - Executes transfer with `kv_trans_v2_for_p_node()` using Triton kernels
  - Monitors health via `is_trans_process_health()` flag

### KV Transfer Workflow

1. **Task Creation**: Backend calls `_alloc_kv_move_task()` after prefill completion
   ```python
   kv_move_task = KVMoveTask(
       group_request_id=batch.reqs[0].group_req_id,
       prefill_node_id=self.world_size,
       decode_node_id=decode_node_id,
       decode_node_ip=decode_node_ip,
       move_kv_len=need_move_len
   )
   self.info_queue.put(kv_move_task)
   ```

2. **Connection Setup**: `KVMoveManager.task_dispatcher_loop()` creates or reuses connection
   ```python
   trans_obj = self.trans_connect_objs.get(decode_node_id, None)
   if trans_obj is None:
       trans_obj = KVTransConnectObj(...)
       self.trans_connect_objs[decode_node_id] = trans_obj
   ```

3. **Resource Allocation**: Decode node allocates KV slots via RPyC
   ```python
   dp_tasks_ans = decode_kv_move_rpyc_client.request_data_transfer(dp_tasks)
   ```

4. **Data Transfer**: `KVTransProcess` transfers via NCCL P2P
   ```python
   cur_mem.send_to_decode_node_p2p(move_tasks, mem_managers, ...)
   ```

5. **Cleanup**: Remove from RadixCache after transfer
   ```python
   self.radix_cache.delete_prefill_reqs_node([req.group_req_id])
   ```

Sources: [lightllm/server/router/model_infer/model_rpc.py:123-179](), [lightllm/server/router/manager.py:202-209](), [lightllm/server/router/model_infer/mode_backend/__init__.py:22-23]()

## Decode Node Implementation

The decode node receives KV cache data from prefill nodes and performs iterative token generation using the transferred context.

### Process Architecture

**Decode Node Component Interactions**

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Main Process"
        RouterManager["RouterManager"] --> ModelRpcClient["ModelRpcClient"]
        ModelRpcClient -->|RPC via Events| ModelRpcServer["ModelRpcServer"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Inference Process"
        ModelRpcServer --> Backend["DecodeNode<br/>or DPForDecodeNode"]
        Backend --> Model["TpPartBaseModel.forward()"]
        Backend -->|Put TransTaskList| InfoQueue["mp.Queue (info_queue)"]
        Backend -->|Read from| RadixCache["RadixCache"]
    end
    
    subgraph "KV Move Manager Process"
        InfoQueue -->|Get TransTaskList| KVMoveManager["DecodeKVMoveManager"]
        KVMoveManager --> RPyCServer["rpyc.ThreadedServer<br/>(pd_decode_rpyc_port)"]
        RPyCServer -->|RPC Call| RequestHandler["exposed_request_data_transfer()"]
        RequestHandler --> AllocLogic["_dp_alloc_to_frozen_some_tokens()"]
        AllocLogic -->|Test Alloc| InferRpc["PDDecodeInferRpcServer"]
        InferRpc -->|Lock| RouterLock["g_router_lock"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Transfer Processes (per GPU)"
        TransProcess["KVTransProcess"] --> NCCLInit["PyNcclCommunicator.init()"]
        NCCLInit --> P2PGroup["NCCL P2P Group"]
        P2PGroup -->|recv()| PrefillNode["Prefill Node"]
        TransProcess -->|Access| MemQueue["mem_queue[device_id]"]
        TransProcess --> ReceiveKernel["kv_trans_v2_for_d_node()"]
    end
    
    AllocLogic -->|Success| TransTaskList["TransTaskList"]
    TransTaskList -->|Put| TransProcess
    ReceiveKernel -->|Write| MemManager["MemoryManager.kv_buffer"]
    MemManager -.->|Shared| MemQueue
    
    subgraph "Task State Management"
        RequestHandler -->|Store| TaskCache["g_kv_move_task_cache"]
        TransProcess -->|Update| SuccessCache["g_success_kv_move_task_cache"]
        Backend -->|Check| SuccessCache
    end
```

### Key Components

**Backend Classes:**
- **`DecodeNode`**: Single DP decode backend
  - Implements `_router_filter_get_can_run_reqs()` to check KV transfer completion
  - Uses `g_success_kv_move_task_cache` to verify ready requests
  - Calls `_check_and_del_mem_manager_buf_without_router_lock()` for cleanup

- **`DPForDecodeNode`**: Multi-DP decode backend with distributed scheduling
  - Extends `DecodeNode` with DP-aware request filtering
  - Coordinates across DP ranks for resource allocation

**KV Receive Management:**
- **`DecodeKVMoveManager`**: RPyC service coordinator started by `start_decode_kv_move_manager_process()`
  - Runs `rpyc.ThreadedServer` on `args.pd_decode_rpyc_port`
  - Exposes `exposed_request_data_transfer()` for prefill node RPyC calls
  - Manages global task caches: `g_kv_move_task_cache` and `g_success_kv_move_task_cache`
  - Implements `_start_trans_processes()` to create `KVTransProcess` workers

- **`PDDecodeInferRpcServer`**: Inference process RPC interface
  - Provides `dp_alloc_to_frozen_some_tokens()` for memory allocation testing
  - Uses `g_router_lock` to synchronize with router during allocation
  - Calls `mem_manager.alloc_token_slots_freezed()` to reserve KV slots

- **`KVTransProcess`**: NCCL receive worker (one per GPU)
  - Initializes with `_init_nccl()` to establish P2P group with prefill node
  - Receives data via `kv_trans_v2_for_d_node()` Triton kernel
  - Processes tasks from `trans_task_list_queue`

### Resource Allocation Flow

**Token Slot Allocation:**

1. **Prefill Node Request**: Calls `decode_kv_move_rpyc_client.request_data_transfer(dp_tasks)`

2. **DP Rank Selection**: `DecodeKVMoveManager._dp_alloc_to_frozen_some_tokens()` tests allocation
   ```python
   for test_index in range(self.dp_size_in_node):
       dp_tasks_ans = self.decode_infer_rpyc[test_index].dp_alloc_to_frozen_some_tokens(dp_tasks)
       if dp_tasks_ans is not None:
           return dp_tasks_ans  # Found available DP rank
   ```

3. **Frozen Allocation**: `PDDecodeInferRpcServer.dp_alloc_to_frozen_some_tokens()`
   ```python
   with g_router_lock.obj:
       decode_token_indexes = self.mem_manager.alloc_token_slots_freezed(need_alloc_token_num)
       if decode_token_indexes is not None:
           task.decode_token_indexes = decode_token_indexes
           task.move_kv_len = len(decode_token_indexes)
   ```

4. **Task Tracking**: Store in `g_kv_move_task_cache[group_request_id]`

5. **Transfer Execution**: `KVTransProcess` receives and writes to allocated slots

6. **Completion**: Move to `g_success_kv_move_task_cache` for backend consumption

### Integration with Inference

The decode backend checks transfer status before scheduling:

```python
def _router_filter_get_can_run_reqs(self, batch: Batch):
    can_run_list = []
    for req in batch.reqs:
        if req.group_req_id in g_success_kv_move_task_cache:
            # KV transfer complete, can decode
            can_run_list.append(req)
    return can_run_list
```

Sources: [lightllm/server/router/model_infer/mode_backend/__init__.py:20-21](), [lightllm/server/router/manager.py:217-223](), [lightllm/server/router/model_infer/model_rpc.py:139-149]()

## PD Master Coordination

The PD master serves as the central coordinator, receiving client requests and orchestrating the prefill/decode workflow across distributed nodes. It does not perform inference itself.

### Request Flow

**Complete PD Separation Request Lifecycle**

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant PDMaster as "PD Master<br/>(HttpServerManagerForPDMaster)"
    participant PrefillHTTP as "Prefill Node<br/>(HttpServerManager)"
    participant PrefillRouter as "Prefill Router"
    participant PrefillKVMove as "PrefillKVMoveManager"
    participant DecodeKVMove as "DecodeKVMoveManager"
    participant DecodeRouter as "Decode Router"
    participant DecodeHTTP as "Decode HTTP"
    
    Client->>PDMaster: POST /generate
    PDMaster->>PDMaster: generate_request_id()
    PDMaster->>PrefillHTTP: Forward to selected prefill node
    
    PrefillHTTP->>PrefillHTTP: HttpServerManager.generate()
    PrefillHTTP->>PrefillRouter: ZMQ PUSH GroupReqIndexes
    PrefillRouter->>PrefillRouter: Run prefill inference
    
    PrefillRouter->>PrefillKVMove: Put KVMoveTask to info_queue
    PrefillKVMove->>DecodeKVMove: RPyC: request_data_transfer()
    DecodeKVMove->>DecodeKVMove: _dp_alloc_to_frozen_some_tokens()
    DecodeKVMove-->>PrefillKVMove: Return allocated slots
    
    PrefillKVMove->>DecodeKVMove: NCCL P2P: send KV cache
    DecodeKVMove->>DecodeKVMove: Mark in g_success_kv_move_task_cache
    
    PrefillRouter->>PrefillHTTP: First token via ZMQ PUB
    PrefillHTTP->>PDMaster: Stream first token + metadata
    PDMaster->>Client: Stream first token
    
    PDMaster->>DecodeHTTP: Forward to decode node
    DecodeHTTP->>DecodeRouter: Continue generation
    DecodeRouter->>DecodeRouter: Check g_success_kv_move_task_cache
    DecodeRouter->>DecodeHTTP: Generate tokens
    DecodeHTTP->>PDMaster: Stream tokens
    PDMaster->>Client: Stream tokens to client
```

### Master Node Architecture

The PD master uses a specialized HTTP server without inference components:

**PD Master Process Structure:**

```python
# From api_start.py: pd_master_start()
def pd_master_start(args):
    # Generate unique node ID for multi-master scenarios
    if args.config_server_host and args.config_server_port:
        args.pd_node_id = uuid.uuid4().int
    else:
        args.pd_node_id = 0
    
    # Start only metric manager (no router, no model processes)
    process_manager.start_submodule_processes(
        start_funcs=[start_metric_manager],
        start_args=[(args,)]
    )
    
    # Start HTTP server with single worker
    command = [
        "gunicorn", "--workers", "1",
        "--worker-class", "uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker",
        "--preload", "lightllm.server.api_http:app"
    ]
```

**Key Differences from Normal Mode:**
- No `start_router_process()` - no local inference scheduling
- No `start_model_process()` - no GPU model loading
- No `start_detokenization_process()` - tokens decoded on worker nodes
- Single Gunicorn worker with `--preload` for efficiency
- Optional health monitor with `start_health_check_process()`

### Node Selection Strategies

The PD master selects prefill/decode nodes using configurable strategies:

```python
# From api_cli.py
--select_p_d_node_strategy: ["random", "round_robin", "adaptive_load"]
```

**Strategy Implementations:**
- **`round_robin`**: Cyclic selection across registered nodes
- **`random`**: Random selection for load distribution
- **`adaptive_load`**: Select nodes based on current token load metrics (recommended)

### Multi-Master Support via Config Server

For high-concurrency deployments, multiple PD masters can be coordinated via `config_server`:

```python
# Config server mode
--run_mode config_server
--config_server_host 0.0.0.0
--config_server_port 8888

# PD master registers with config server
--config_server_host <config_server_ip>
--config_server_port 8888
```

The config server maintains a registry of active PD master nodes for client discovery and load balancing.

Sources: [lightllm/server/api_start.py:371-431](), [lightllm/server/api_cli.py:46-51](), [lightllm/server/api_server.py:10-15]()

## KV Cache Transfer Mechanism

The KV transfer system is the core of PD separation, enabling efficient movement of key-value cache data between prefill and decode nodes.

### Transfer Architecture

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Prefill Side"
        PrefillMem["MemoryManager"] --> KVBuffer1["kv_buffer[layer, token, head, dim]"]
        KVBuffer1 --> MoveBuffer1["kv_move_buffer"]
        MoveBuffer1 --> P2PTransfer["kv_trans_v2_for_p_node()"]
        TransProcess1["KVTransProcess"] --> NCCLSend["nccl_comm.send()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "NCCL P2P Channel"
        NCCLSend --> NCCLRecv["nccl_comm.recv()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Decode Side"
        NCCLRecv --> TransProcess2["KVTransProcess"]
        TransProcess2 --> P2PReceive["kv_trans_v2_for_d_node()"]
        P2PReceive --> MoveBuffer2["kv_move_buffer"]
        MoveBuffer2 --> KVBuffer2["kv_buffer[layer, token, head, dim]"]
        KVBuffer2 --> DecodeMem["MemoryManager"]
    end
```

### Transfer Methods

The system supports two KV transfer methods:

1. **Standard Transfer**: Uses tensor copying and NCCL broadcast
2. **P2P Transfer**: Uses optimized Triton kernels with direct memory access

```python
# P2P transfer method selection
if kv_trans_use_p2p():
    cur_mem.send_to_decode_node_p2p(move_tasks, mem_managers, dp_size_in_node, nccl_comm)
else:
    cur_mem.send_to_decode_node(move_tasks, mem_managers, dp_size_in_node, nccl_comm)
```

### Memory Buffer Management

Each memory manager allocates specialized buffers for KV transfer:

- **`kv_move_buffer`**: Temporary buffer for KV data during transfer
- **`kv_move_buf_indexes`**: Index mapping for efficient data copying
- **`token_dim_size`**: Cached dimension size for buffer calculations

Sources: [lightllm/common/mem_manager.py:86-241](), [lightllm/common/deepseek2_mem_manager.py:31-215](), [lightllm/server/router/model_infer/mode_backend/continues_batch/pd_mode/prefill_node_impl/prefill_trans_process.py:21-155]()

### Health Monitoring

Each node implements health monitoring to ensure system reliability:

```python
# Health check implementation
def check_trans_process_loop(self):
    while True:
        for device_id in range(self.node_world_size):
            if not self.kv_trans_processes[device_id].is_trans_process_health():
                # Trigger system restart on health failure
                os.kill(os.getppid(), signal.SIGKILL)
        time.sleep(10.0)
```

### Resource Cleanup

The system implements comprehensive cleanup mechanisms:

- **Connection Cleanup**: Automatic removal of dead transport objects
- **Memory Recovery**: Garbage collection after connection failures
- **Process Termination**: Recursive process killing on errors

### Memory Management

The system requires additional memory allocation for KV transfer buffers:

```python
# Additional memory allocation for PD mode
def alloc_kv_move_buffer(self, max_req_total_len):
    self.kv_move_buffer = torch.empty(
        (1, max_req_total_len + 8, 2 * self.head_num, self.head_dim),
        dtype=self.dtype, device="cuda"
    )
```

### Performance Tuning

Key parameters for performance optimization:

- **Transfer Batch Size**: `KV_MOVE_MAX_NUM = 16` limits concurrent transfers
- **Timeout Settings**: 6-second timeout for unused KV cache cleanup
- **Channel Configuration**: `NCCL_MAX_NCHANNELS = 2` for transfer processes

## Purpose and Scope

NIXL (Network Inference with eXtra Latency optimization) Mode is an enhanced variant of Prefill-Decode separation that optimizes distributed inference through chunked KV cache transfer, improved load balancing, and WebSocket-based coordination. This page covers the NIXL-specific architecture, components, and operational flow.

For basic Prefill-Decode separation concepts, see [Prefill-Decode Separation](#7.4). For general distributed deployment patterns, see [Run Modes and Deployment Types](#7.1). For standard PD Master coordination, see [Prefill-Decode Separation](#7.4).

**Key Features:**
- **Chunked KV Transfer**: Incremental transmission of KV cache data to avoid blocking prefill operations
- **Enhanced Load Balancing**: Dynamic decode node selection based on ready KV cache state
- **WebSocket Coordination**: Real-time communication between prefill nodes and PD Master for node assignment
- **Task-Based Transfer**: Explicit success/failure tracking for KV transfer operations

---

## Architecture Overview

NIXL mode extends the standard P-D architecture with specialized node types and transfer mechanisms. The system uses `NodeRole.NP` (NIXL Prefill) and `NodeRole.ND` (NIXL Decode) instead of the standard `P` and `D` roles.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Client Layer"
        Client["External Client"]
    end
    
    subgraph "PD Master (Coordinator)"
        PDMaster["PD Master Server<br/>run_mode=pd_master"]
        UploadWS["WebSocket Endpoint<br/>/pd_upload"]
        NodeRegistry["Node Registry<br/>NP and ND nodes"]
        LoadBalancer["NIXL Load Balancer<br/>Decode node selection"]
    end
    
    subgraph "NIXL Prefill Cluster"
        NP1["NIXL Prefill Node 1<br/>run_mode=nixl_prefill<br/>HttpServerManager"]
        NP2["NIXL Prefill Node 2<br/>run_mode=nixl_prefill"]
        
        subgraph "NP Backend"
            NPBackend["NIXLChunckedPrefillForPrefillNode<br/>or NIXLDPChunkedForPrefillNode"]
            NPKVMove["KV Move Manager<br/>Chunked transfer"]
            NPTransBuffer["shm_nixl_trans_io_buffer<br/>Task status tracking"]
        end
    end
    
    subgraph "NIXL Decode Cluster"
        ND1["NIXL Decode Node 1<br/>run_mode=nixl_decode<br/>HttpServerManager"]
        ND2["NIXL Decode Node 2<br/>run_mode=nixl_decode"]
        
        subgraph "ND Backend"
            NDBackend["NIXLDecodeNode<br/>or NIXLDPForDecodeNode"]
            NDKVMove["KV Move Manager<br/>Receive and load"]
            NDReadyKV["Ready KV Length<br/>Per-request tracking"]
        end
    end
    
    Client -->|HTTP Request| PDMaster
    PDMaster -->|Route to NP| NP1
    PDMaster -->|Route to NP| NP2
    
    NP1 -->|1. Upload prompt_ids<br/>via WebSocket| UploadWS
    UploadWS -->|2. Assign ND node<br/>NIXLDecodeNodeInfo| NP1
    
    NP1 --> NPBackend
    NPBackend --> NPKVMove
    NPKVMove -->|Chunked KV Transfer| NDKVMove
    NPKVMove -->|Task status| NPTransBuffer
    
    NDKVMove --> NDBackend
    NDBackend --> ND1
    
    ND1 -->|Stream results| PDMaster
    PDMaster -->|Stream results| Client
    
    LoadBalancer -.->|Select based on<br/>ready_kv_len| ND1
    LoadBalancer -.->|Select based on<br/>ready_kv_len| ND2
    
    style PDMaster fill:#ff9999
    style NP1 fill:#99ccff
    style ND1 fill:#99ff99
    style LoadBalancer fill:#ffeb99
```

**NIXL Mode vs Standard P-D Mode:**

| Aspect | Standard P-D | NIXL Mode |
|--------|-------------|-----------|
| Node Roles | `NodeRole.P`, `NodeRole.D` | `NodeRole.NP`, `NodeRole.ND` |
| KV Transfer | Bulk transfer after prefill | Chunked incremental transfer |
| Coordination | Basic routing | WebSocket + upload/download flow |
| Load Balancing | Static assignment | Dynamic based on ready KV state |
| Transfer Tracking | Implicit | Explicit task success/failure |
| Prefill Optimization | May wait for full transfer | Can skip if decode node ready |

Sources: [lightllm/server/httpserver/manager.py:105-106](), [lightllm/server/router/model_infer/model_rpc.py:125-149]()

## Communication Flow

### Request Lifecycle in NIXL Mode

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant PDMaster as PD Master
    participant NP as NIXL Prefill Node
    participant ND as NIXL Decode Node
    
    Client->>PDMaster: HTTP Request
    PDMaster->>NP: Route to prefill
    
    Note over NP: Encode prompt
    NP->>NP: tokenizer.encode(prompt)
    NP->>NP: prompt_ids = [tok1, tok2, ..., tokN]
    
    Note over NP,PDMaster: WebSocket Upload Phase
    NP->>PDMaster: WS: Upload (group_req_id, prompt_ids)
    Note over PDMaster: Select decode node<br/>based on load
    PDMaster->>NP: WS: NIXLDecodeNodeInfo<br/>(node_id, ready_kv_len)
    
    alt ready_kv_len == len(prompt_ids) - 1
        Note over NP: Skip prefill entirely
        NP->>NP: Raise NixlPrefillNodeStopGenToken
    else ready_kv_len < len(prompt_ids) - 1
        Note over NP: Perform prefill
        NP->>NP: Prefill from ready_kv_len to end
        
        loop For each chunk
            NP->>ND: Transfer KV chunk
            ND->>ND: Load chunk to GPU
            ND->>NP: NIXLChunckedTransTaskRet(success)
            NP->>NP: Update nixl_pd_task_sunccess_num
        end
        
        NP->>ND: First token info (id, logprob)
    end
    
    Note over ND: Decode phase
    ND->>ND: Check all tasks complete
    ND->>ND: Prefill first token to output
    
    loop Until finished
        ND->>ND: Generate next token
        ND->>PDMaster: Stream token
        PDMaster->>Client: Stream token
    end
    
    ND->>PDMaster: Finish status
    PDMaster->>Client: Complete response
```

**Phase Breakdown:**

1. **Upload Phase** ([lightllm/server/httpserver/manager.py:295-308]()):
   - Prefill node encodes prompt
   - Uploads `(group_req_id, prompt_ids)` via WebSocket
   - Waits for `NIXLDecodeNodeInfo` with timeout (80s)

2. **Optimization Check** ([lines 313-316]()):
   - If `ready_kv_len == len(prompt_ids) - 1`, skip prefill
   - Raises `NixlPrefillNodeStopGenToken` exception

3. **Chunked Transfer** ([lightllm/server/router/model_infer/mode_backend/base_backend.py:384-415]()):
   - Prefill node initiates transfer tasks
   - Each chunk tracked via `NIXLChunckedTransTaskRet`
   - Decode node updates `nixl_pd_task_sunccess_num` or `nixl_pd_task_failed_num`

4. **Decode Preparation** ([lines 397-414]()):
   - Decode node receives first token from prefill
   - Prefills `req_to_next_token_ids` with first token
   - Updates request state via `InferReqUpdatePack`

Sources: [lightllm/server/httpserver/manager.py:295-316](), [lightllm/server/router/model_infer/mode_backend/base_backend.py:384-415]()

### Shared Memory Coordination

NIXL mode uses a dedicated shared memory buffer for transfer status updates:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Shared Memory Structures"
        NormalBuffer["ShmObjsIOBuffer<br/>(default)<br/>Request objects<br/>Abort commands"]
        NIXLBuffer["ShmObjsIOBuffer<br/>tail_str='nixl'<br/>NIXLChunckedTransTaskRet"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Prefill Process"

        PrefillRead["_read_nixl_trans_io_buffer<br/>Read task status"]
        PrefillUpdate["Update InferReq counters<br/>nixl_pd_task_sunccess_num<br/>nixl_pd_task_failed_num"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Decode Process"
```

## Chunked KV Transfer Mechanism

### Transfer Process

Unlike standard P-D mode which transfers all KV cache after prefill completes, NIXL mode performs incremental chunked transfer:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Prefill Node KV Memory"
        PrefillKV["KV Cache Buffer<br/>req_to_token_indexs[req_idx]"]
        StartIdx["nixl_trans_kv_start_index<br/>(from ready_kv_len)"]
        EndIdx["cur_kv_len<br/>(after prefill)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Transfer Logic"
        ChunkSize["Chunk Size<br/>(configurable)"]
        Loop["For chunk in<br/>[start_idx : end_idx]"]
        TaskCreate["Create Transfer Task<br/>NIXLChunckedTransTask"]
        Queue["Task Queue<br/>to KV Move Manager"]
    end
    
    subgraph "KV Move Manager"
        Sender["Send Chunk<br/>Network/RPyC"]
        RetCreate["Create Return Status<br/>NIXLChunckedTransTaskRet"]
        WriteBuffer["Write to<br/>shm_nixl_trans_io_buffer"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Decode Node"
        Receiver["Receive Chunk"]
        LoadGPU["Load to GPU<br/>req_to_token_indexs"]
        UpdateReady["Update ready_kv_len"]
        ReadBuffer["Read from<br/>shm_nixl_trans_io_buffer"]
    end
    
    PrefillKV --> StartIdx
    PrefillKV --> EndIdx
    StartIdx --> Loop
    EndIdx --> Loop
    ChunkSize --> Loop
    Loop --> TaskCreate
    TaskCreate --> Queue
    Queue --> Sender
    
    Sender --> Receiver
    Receiver --> LoadGPU
    LoadGPU --> UpdateReady
    
    Sender --> RetCreate
    RetCreate --> WriteBuffer
    WriteBuffer --> ReadBuffer
    
    style TaskCreate fill:#99ccff
    style RetCreate fill:#99ff99
    style WriteBuffer fill:#ffeb99
```

**Transfer Initiation** ([lightllm/server/router/model_infer/mode_backend/base_backend.py:67]()):
- Callback function: `nixl_prefill_chuncked_handle_func`
- Called during `InferReqUpdatePack.handle()` in prefill phase
- Parameters: `(InferReq, int, float, int)` - request, token_id, logprob, chunk_index

**Status Tracking** ([lightllm/server/router/model_infer/infer_batch.py:337-340]()):
```python
self.nixl_trans_kv_start_index: int = 0      # Where to start transfer
self.nixl_pd_task_num: int = 0               # Total tasks
self.nixl_pd_task_sunccess_num: int = 0      # Successful transfers
self.nixl_pd_task_failed_num: int = 0        # Failed transfers
```

**Completion Check** ([lightllm/server/router/model_infer/mode_backend/base_backend.py:389-394]()):
```python
if obj.request_id in g_infer_context.requests_mapping:
    req: InferReq = g_infer_context.requests_mapping[obj.request_id]
    if obj.has_error:
        req.nixl_pd_task_failed_num += 1
    else:
        req.nixl_pd_task_sunccess_num += 1
```

Sources: [lightllm/server/router/model_infer/mode_backend/base_backend.py:67, 384-415](), [lightllm/server/router/model_infer/infer_batch.py:336-341]()

### First Token Handling

NIXL mode optimizes decode startup by prefilling the first generated token:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Prefill as Prefill Node
    participant KVMove as KV Move Manager
    participant Buffer as shm_nixl_trans_io_buffer
    participant Decode as Decode Node Backend
    participant ReqMgr as ReqManager
    
    Note over Prefill: Complete prefill
    Prefill->>Prefill: Generate first token
    Prefill->>KVMove: Send (first_token_id, logprob)
    
    KVMove->>Buffer: Write NIXLChunckedTransTaskRet<br/>first_gen_token_id<br/>first_gen_token_logprob
    Buffer->>Buffer: Set ready flag
    
    Note over Decode: Read transfer status
    Decode->>Buffer: Check is_ready()
    Decode->>Buffer: Read NIXLChunckedTransTaskRet
    
    alt obj.first_gen_token_id is not None
        Note over Decode: Decode node receives first token
        Decode->>Decode: assert req.cur_output_len == 0
        Decode->>ReqMgr: req_to_next_token_ids[req_idx, 0:1]<br/>.fill_(first_gen_token_id)
        Decode->>Decode: req.cur_output_len += 1
        Decode->>Decode: InferReqUpdatePack.handle()
    end
```

**Implementation** ([lightllm/server/router/model_infer/mode_backend/base_backend.py:397-414]()):
```python
if self.is_nixl_decode_mode:
    if obj.first_gen_token_id is not None:
        assert req.cur_output_len == 0
        req.cur_output_len += 1
        req_to_next_token_ids = (
            self.model.req_manager.req_sampling_params_manager.req_to_next_token_ids
        )
        req_to_next_token_ids[req.req_idx, 0:1].fill_(obj.first_gen_token_id)
        torch.cuda.current_stream().synchronize()
        InferReqUpdatePack(req_obj=req, output_len=req.cur_output_len).handle(
            next_token_id=obj.first_gen_token_id,
            next_token_logprob=obj.first_gen_token_logprob,
            eos_ids=self.eos_id,
            extra_post_req_handle_func=None,
            is_master_in_dp=self.is_master_in_dp,
            nixl_prefill_chuncked_handle_func=None,
        )
```

This allows the decode node to skip waiting for a full decode cycle and immediately continue generation.

Sources: [lightllm/server/router/model_infer/mode_backend/base_backend.py:396-414]()

## Load Balancing and Optimization

### Ready KV Length Optimization

NIXL mode's key optimization is tracking `ready_kv_len` to skip redundant prefill work:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "PD Master Selection Logic"
        SelectND["Select Decode Node"]
        QueryReadyKV["Query ready_kv_len<br/>for request prefix"]
        FindMatch["Find node with<br/>longest ready_kv_len"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Prefill Node Decision"
        ReceiveInfo["Receive NIXLDecodeNodeInfo"]
        Compare["Compare:<br/>ready_kv_len vs<br/>len(prompt_ids) - 1"]
        SkipPrefill["Skip Prefill<br/>Raise NixlPrefillNodeStopGenToken"]
        PartialPrefill["Partial Prefill<br/>from ready_kv_len"]
        FullPrefill["Full Prefill<br/>from 0"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Scenarios"
        S1["Scenario 1:<br/>ready_kv_len == len(prompt_ids) - 1<br/>Decode node has full cache"]
        S2["Scenario 2:<br/>ready_kv_len > 0<br/>Partial cache hit"]
        S3["Scenario 3:<br/>ready_kv_len == 0<br/>No cache"]
    end
    
    SelectND --> QueryReadyKV
    QueryReadyKV --> FindMatch
    FindMatch --> ReceiveInfo
    
    ReceiveInfo --> Compare
    Compare -->|Equal| S1
    Compare -->|Greater than 0| S2
    Compare -->|Zero| S3
    
    S1 --> SkipPrefill
    S2 --> PartialPrefill
    S3 --> FullPrefill
    
    style S1 fill:#99ff99
    style S2 fill:#ffeb99
    style S3 fill:#ffcccc
```

**Skip Prefill Logic** ([lightllm/server/httpserver/manager.py:313-316]()):
```python
if decode_node_info.ready_kv_len == len(prompt_ids) - 1:
    # Decode node already has all needed KV cache
    # No prefill required
    raise NixlPrefillNodeStopGenToken(group_request_id=group_request_id)
```

**Partial Prefill** ([lightllm/server/router/model_infer/infer_batch.py:367-368]()):
```python
if self.sampling_param.nixl_decode_node is not None:
    self.nixl_trans_kv_start_index = self.sampling_param.nixl_decode_node.ready_kv_len
```
Transfer starts from `ready_kv_len` instead of 0, saving bandwidth and time.

Sources: [lightllm/server/httpserver/manager.py:310-316](), [lightllm/server/router/model_infer/infer_batch.py:366-368]()

### Request Filtering for Transfer Readiness

Decode nodes filter requests until KV transfer completes:

```mermaid
    subgraph "Request Classification"

```

**Filter Implementation** ([lightllm/server/router/model_infer/mode_backend/base_backend.py:443-449]()):
```python
def _filter_not_ready_reqs(self, req_ids: List[int]) -> List[InferReq]:
    """
    Filter out requests with incomplete KV transfer.
    Used in NIXL PD mode to check transfer status.
    """
    return [g_infer_context.requests_mapping[request_id] for request_id in req_ids]
```

This method is overridden in NIXL backend implementations to add transfer completion checks.

## Configuration and Deployment

### Run Mode Selection

NIXL mode is enabled through the `run_mode` argument:

```python
# NIXL Prefill Node
python -m lightllm.server.api_server \
    --run_mode nixl_prefill \
    --model_dir /path/to/model \
    --tp 4 \
    --dp 1 \
    ...

# NIXL Decode Node
python -m lightllm.server.api_server \
    --run_mode nixl_decode \
    --model_dir /path/to/model \
    --tp 4 \
    --dp 1 \
    ...

# PD Master (same for both standard and NIXL)
python -m lightllm.server.api_server \
    --run_mode pd_master \
    --port 8000 \
    ...
```

Sources: [lightllm/server/api_server.py:10-15]()

### Backend Selection Logic

Backend classes are selected based on `run_mode` and `dp` settings:

```mermaid

    CheckMode{"run_mode?"}
```

**Implementation** ([lightllm/server/router/model_infer/model_rpc.py:123-149]()):
```python
is_nixl_prefill_node = self.args.run_mode == "nixl_prefill"
is_nixl_decode_node = self.args.run_mode == "nixl_decode"

if is_nixl_prefill_node:
    if self.args.dp > 1:
        self.backend = NIXLDPChunkedForPrefillNode(self.info_queue, self.mem_queue)
    else:
        self.backend = NIXLChunckedPrefillForPrefillNode(self.info_queue, self.mem_queue)

elif is_nixl_decode_node:
    if self.args.dp > 1:
        self.backend = NIXLDPForDecodeNode(self.info_queue, self.mem_queue)
    else:
        self.backend = NIXLDecodeNode(self.info_queue, self.mem_queue)
```

## Comparison with Standard P-D Mode

| Feature | Standard P-D Mode | NIXL Mode |
|---------|-------------------|-----------|
| **Node Roles** | `NodeRole.P`, `NodeRole.D` | `NodeRole.NP`, `NodeRole.ND` |
| **Coordination** | Simple routing | WebSocket upload/download flow |
| **KV Transfer** | Bulk after prefill | Chunked incremental |
| **Transfer Tracking** | Implicit | Explicit task status (`NIXLChunckedTransTaskRet`) |
| **Prefill Skip** | Not supported | Skip if `ready_kv_len == len(prompt_ids) - 1` |
| **First Token** | Standard decode cycle | Prefilled from prefill node |
| **Load Balancing** | Basic | Enhanced with ready KV state |
| **Shared Memory** | `ShmObjsIOBuffer` | Additional `shm_nixl_trans_io_buffer` |
| **Backend Classes** | `ChunckedPrefillForPrefillNode`, `DecodeNode` | `NIXLChunckedPrefillForPrefillNode`, `NIXLDecodeNode` |
| **Transfer Start** | After full prefill | During prefill (chunked) |
| **Error Handling** | Basic | Per-chunk success/failure tracking |

---

## Key Data Structures

### NIXLDecodeNodeInfo

Passed from PD Master to prefill node via WebSocket to assign decode node:

**Fields:**
- `node_id`: Identifier of assigned decode node
- `ready_kv_len`: Length of KV cache already available on decode node
- Additional routing information

**Usage** ([lightllm/server/httpserver/manager.py:310-311]()):
```python
decode_node_info: NIXLDecodeNodeInfo = nixl_pd_event.decode_node_info
sampling_params.nixl_params.set(pickle.dumps(decode_node_info))
```

Sources: [lightllm/server/httpserver/manager.py:310-311](), [lightllm/server/router/model_infer/infer_batch.py:274-277]()

### NIXLChunckedTransTaskRet

Transfer task completion status written to shared memory:

**Fields:**
- `request_id`: Request identifier
- `has_error`: Boolean indicating transfer failure
- `first_gen_token_id`: Optional first generated token
- `first_gen_token_logprob`: Optional log probability

**Processing** ([lightllm/server/router/model_infer/mode_backend/base_backend.py:385-394]()):
```python
cmds: List[NIXLChunckedTransTaskRet] = self.shm_nixl_trans_io_buffer.read_obj()
for obj in cmds:
    if obj.request_id in g_infer_context.requests_mapping:
        req: InferReq = g_infer_context.requests_mapping[obj.request_id]
        if obj.has_error:
            req.nixl_pd_task_failed_num += 1
        else:
            req.nixl_pd_task_sunccess_num += 1
```

## Error Handling and Timeouts

### WebSocket Upload Timeout

Prefill nodes have a timeout when waiting for decode node assignment:

```python
await asyncio.wait_for(nixl_pd_event.wait(), timeout=80)
```

If timeout occurs, the request is aborted ([lightllm/server/httpserver/manager.py:305-308]()):
```python
except asyncio.TimeoutError:
    logger.error(f"nixl np node wait nixl_pd_event 36s time out, group_req_id {group_request_id}")
    raise Exception(f"group_req_id {group_request_id} wait nixl_pd_event time out")
```

### Transfer Failure Tracking

Each request tracks transfer failures via counters:
- `nixl_pd_task_num`: Total tasks
- `nixl_pd_task_sunccess_num`: Successful transfers
- `nixl_pd_task_failed_num`: Failed transfers

Backend implementations can use these to determine when to retry or abort.

Sources: [lightllm/server/httpserver/manager.py:305-308](), [lightllm/server/router/model_infer/infer_batch.py:337-340]()

---

## Summary

NIXL Mode provides an optimized distributed inference architecture that:

1. **Reduces Latency**: Chunked transfer allows decode to start earlier
2. **Improves Resource Utilization**: Skip redundant prefill work via `ready_kv_len`
3. **Enhances Robustness**: Explicit task tracking with success/failure counters
4. **Enables Better Load Balancing**: PD Master selects decode nodes based on cache state
5. **Maintains Compatibility**: Works with Data Parallel (DP) mode for additional scaling

For deployment, NIXL mode requires:
- PD Master coordinator (same as standard P-D)
- NIXL Prefill nodes (`run_mode=nixl_prefill`)
- NIXL Decode nodes (`run_mode=nixl_decode`)
- WebSocket connectivity between prefill nodes and PD Master
- Shared memory for transfer status coordination

For more details on standard P-D separation, see [Prefill-Decode Separation](#7.4). For PD Master configuration, see [Run Modes and Deployment Types](#7.1).

## Purpose and Scope

Multi-Node Setup enables running LightLLM across multiple physical machines (nodes) to support large models that require distributed inference. This page covers the configuration, initialization, and coordination mechanisms for multi-node deployments with tensor parallelism.

**When to use multi-node setup:**
- Models too large for a single node's GPUs (e.g., >70B parameter models requiring >8 GPUs)
- Scaling tensor parallelism beyond what a single node provides
- Distributing computation across multiple machines for improved throughput

**Related pages:**
- For tensor parallelism concepts and intra-node parallelism, see [Tensor Parallelism](#7.2)
- For P-D separation across nodes, see [Prefill-Decode Separation](#7.4) and [NIXL Mode](#7.5)
- For general deployment configuration, see [Configuration and Command-Line Arguments](#2.3)

**Note:** Multi-node setup is primarily designed for multi-node tensor parallelism (`--nnodes > 1` with `--dp=1`). Multi-node data parallelism is not the primary focus of this configuration.

---

## Configuration Parameters

Multi-node deployment requires several command-line arguments to coordinate nodes and establish communication channels:

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--nnodes` | int | 1 | Total number of nodes in the cluster |
| `--node_rank` | int | 0 | Rank of current node (0 to nnodes-1) |
| `--nccl_host` | str | "127.0.0.1" | Master node IP for NCCL initialization |
| `--nccl_port` | int | 28765 | Port for PyTorch distributed initialization |
| `--multinode_httpmanager_port` | int | 12345 | Port for HTTP manager coordination |
| `--multinode_router_gloo_port` | int | 20001 | Gloo backend port for router coordination |
| `--use_config_server_to_init_nccl` | bool | False | Use config_server TCP store for NCCL init |
| `--tp` | int | 1 | Total tensor parallel size across all nodes |

**Important relationships:**
- `tp` must be divisible by `nnodes` (e.g., `tp=16, nnodes=2` → 8 GPUs per node)
- `node_rank=0` is always the master node
- All nodes must use the same `nccl_port` for a given deployment
- `nccl_host` must be set to the master node's IP address on all worker nodes

**Example configuration for 2-node, 16-GPU deployment:**

```bash
# Node 0 (Master)
python -m lightllm.server.api_server \
    --model_dir /path/to/model \
    --tp 16 \
    --nnodes 2 \
    --node_rank 0 \
    --nccl_host 192.168.1.100 \
    --nccl_port 28765

# Node 1 (Worker)
python -m lightllm.server.api_server \
    --model_dir /path/to/model \
    --tp 16 \
    --nnodes 2 \
    --node_rank 1 \
    --nccl_host 192.168.1.100 \
    --nccl_port 28765
```

Sources: [lightllm/server/api_cli.py:151-164](), [lightllm/server/core/objs/start_args_type.py:40-44]()

---

## Network and NCCL Requirements

### Network Prerequisites

**Required:**
- All nodes must have direct network connectivity
- Low-latency network recommended (InfiniBand or high-speed Ethernet)
- Open firewall ports for all required communication channels

**Port requirements:**
- `nccl_port` for PyTorch distributed initialization
- `multinode_httpmanager_port` for HTTP coordination
- `multinode_router_gloo_port` for router Gloo backend
- Additional ports automatically allocated for model RPC servers

### NCCL Configuration

NCCL (NVIDIA Collective Communications Library) is used for GPU-to-GPU communication across nodes. The initialization happens through PyTorch's distributed package.

**Two initialization modes:**

1. **Standard NCCL init (default):**
   - Uses PyTorch's `tcp://` store
   - Master node (`node_rank=0`) acts as rendezvous point
   - All nodes connect to `nccl_host:nccl_port`

2. **Config server NCCL init:**
   - Set `--use_config_server_to_init_nccl`
   - Uses centralized config_server as TCP store
   - Requires `--config_server_host` and `--config_server_port`
   - Allows multiple independent deployments with unique `nccl_port` values
   - `nccl_host` must equal `config_server_host` in this mode

**NCCL environment variables (optional):**
```bash
export NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0  # Network interface to use
export NCCL_IB_DISABLE=0        # Enable InfiniBand if available
export NCCL_DEBUG=INFO          # Enable debug logging
```

Sources: [lightllm/server/api_cli.py:185-200](), [lightllm/server/api_start.py:95-97]()

---

## Multi-Node Communication Architecture

Multi-node LightLLM establishes several communication channels between nodes:

### Communication Channels Diagram

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Node 0 (Master) - rank 0"
        M_HTTP["HTTP Server<br/>(port 8000)"]
        M_Router["Router Manager"]
        M_Model0["Model RPC<br/>GPU 0"]
        M_Model1["Model RPC<br/>GPU N-1"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Node 1 (Worker) - rank 1"
        W_HTTP["HTTP Server<br/>(port 8000)"]
        W_Router["Router Manager"]
        W_Model0["Model RPC<br/>GPU 0"]
        W_Model1["Model RPC<br/>GPU N-1"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Cross-Node Communication"
        NCCL["NCCL All-Reduce<br/>All GPUs"]
        Gloo["Gloo Backend<br/>Router coordination"]
        ZMQ["ZMQ Socket<br/>Request forwarding"]
        HTTP_Coord["HTTP Coordination<br/>multinode_httpmanager_port"]
    end
    
    M_Model0 -->|"Tensor sync"| NCCL
    M_Model1 -->|"Tensor sync"| NCCL
    W_Model0 -->|"Tensor sync"| NCCL
    W_Model1 -->|"Tensor sync"| NCCL
    
    M_Router -->|"Coordination"| Gloo
    W_Router -->|"Coordination"| Gloo
    
    M_HTTP -->|"Forward reqs"| ZMQ
    ZMQ -->|"To workers"| W_HTTP
    
    M_HTTP -->|"IP exchange"| HTTP_Coord
    W_HTTP -->|"IP exchange"| HTTP_Coord
    
    style NCCL fill:#f9f9f9
    style Gloo fill:#f9f9f9
    style ZMQ fill:#f9f9f9
```

### Channel Purposes

1. **NCCL (GPU-GPU):**
   - All-reduce operations for tensor parallel model weights
   - Broadcast operations for activations during forward pass
   - Reduce-scatter for gradient-like operations
   - Used by all model RPC processes across all nodes

2. **Gloo Backend (Router):**
   - Router manager coordination between nodes
   - Synchronization barriers during request processing
   - Shares routing decisions across nodes
   - Port: `multinode_router_gloo_port`

3. **ZMQ Sockets (Request Flow):**
   - Master node forwards requests to worker nodes
   - Unidirectional: master → workers
   - Used for request distribution in multi-node TP mode

4. **HTTP Coordination:**
   - Initial node IP exchange via `send_and_receive_node_ip()`
   - Node discovery and validation
   - Port: `multinode_httpmanager_port`

Sources: [lightllm/server/router/model_infer/mode_backend/base_backend.py:199-210](), [lightllm/utils/multinode_utils.py]()

## Initialization Sequence

Multi-node initialization follows a carefully orchestrated sequence to ensure all nodes are synchronized before serving requests:

### Initialization Flow Diagram

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Node0 as "Node 0 (Master)"
    participant Node1 as "Node 1 (Worker)"
    participant NCCL as "NCCL Store"
    participant Network as "Network Layer"
    
    Note over Node0,Node1: Phase 1: Parameter Validation
    Node0->>Node0: Validate args<br/>(nnodes, tp, node_rank)
    Node1->>Node1: Validate args<br/>(nnodes, tp, node_rank)
    
    Note over Node0,Node1: Phase 2: Network Discovery
    Node0->>Network: Start HTTP server<br/>multinode_httpmanager_port
    Node1->>Network: Start HTTP server<br/>multinode_httpmanager_port
    Node0->>Network: send_and_receive_node_ip()
    Node1->>Network: send_and_receive_node_ip()
    Network-->>Node0: All node IPs
    Network-->>Node1: All node IPs
    
    Note over Node0,Node1: Phase 3: NCCL Initialization
    Node0->>NCCL: Create TCP store<br/>nccl_host:nccl_port
    Node1->>NCCL: Connect to TCP store<br/>nccl_host:nccl_port
    NCCL-->>Node0: Group initialized
    NCCL-->>Node1: Group initialized
    
    Note over Node0,Node1: Phase 4: Process Group Setup
    Node0->>Node0: init_distributed_env()
    Node1->>Node1: init_distributed_env()
    Node0->>Node0: create_new_group_for_current_node()
    Node1->>Node1: create_new_group_for_current_node()
    
    Note over Node0,Node1: Phase 5: Model Loading
    Node0->>Node0: Load model shards<br/>(GPUs 0 to N-1)
    Node1->>Node1: Load model shards<br/>(GPUs N to 2N-1)
    
    Note over Node0,Node1: Phase 6: Synchronization Barrier
    Node0->>NCCL: dist.barrier()
    Node1->>NCCL: dist.barrier()
    NCCL-->>Node0: All ready
    NCCL-->>Node1: All ready
    
    Note over Node0,Node1: Ready to Serve
```

### Key Initialization Steps

**1. Parameter Validation** [lightllm/server/api_start.py:63-79]()
- Validates `nnodes`, `node_rank`, `tp` parameters
- Checks `tp % nnodes == 0` (GPUs per node must be equal)
- Sets unique server name based on `nccl_port` and `node_rank`

**2. Port Allocation** [lightllm/server/api_start.py:226-241]()
```python
node_world_size = args.tp // args.nnodes
can_use_ports = alloc_can_use_network_port(
    num=8 + node_world_size + args.visual_dp * args.visual_tp, 
    used_nccl_ports=already_uesd_ports
)
```
Each node allocates identical port sets for:
- Router, detokenization, HTTP server
- Visual/audio/cache servers (if enabled)
- One port per GPU for model RPC

**3. Node IP Exchange** [lightllm/server/api_start.py:271]()
```python
send_and_receive_node_ip(args)
```
- Nodes exchange IP addresses via HTTP coordination port
- Master node collects all worker node IPs
- Enables subsequent cross-node communication

**4. Distributed Environment Initialization** [lightllm/server/router/model_infer/mode_backend/base_backend.py:108]()
```python
init_distributed_env(kvargs)
```
- Calls PyTorch `dist.init_process_group()`
- Backend: "nccl" for GPU operations, "gloo" for CPU operations
- Creates global process group with all ranks across all nodes

**5. Node-Local and Multi-Node Groups** [lightllm/server/router/model_infer/mode_backend/base_backend.py:199-210]()
```python
# Node-local NCCL group (for intra-node coordination)
self.node_nccl_group = create_new_group_for_current_node("nccl")

# Multi-node TP group (for cross-node coordination)
if self.is_multinode_tp:
    self.multinode_tp_nccl_group = dist.new_group(
        [rank for rank in range(self.global_world_size)], 
        backend="nccl"
    )
```

**6. Model Loading and Barrier** [lightllm/server/router/model_infer/mode_backend/base_backend.py:133]()
```python
dist.barrier()  # Synchronize all nodes after loading
```
- Each node loads its assigned model weight shards
- Barrier ensures all nodes finish loading before accepting requests

Sources: [lightllm/server/api_start.py:63-272](), [lightllm/server/router/model_infer/mode_backend/base_backend.py:75-134]()

## Master-Slave Coordination in Multi-Node TP

In multi-node tensor parallelism mode (`nnodes > 1` and `dp == 1`), node 0 acts as the master with special responsibilities:

### Master Node Responsibilities

**Request Reception:**
- Only the master node (`node_rank=0`) exposes the HTTP API on port 8000
- All client requests arrive at the master node
- Worker nodes do not accept direct client connections

**Request Distribution:**
```python
# Check if running in multi-node TP mode
self.is_multinode_tp = self.args.nnodes > 1 and self.args.dp == 1
```
[lightllm/server/router/model_infer/mode_backend/base_backend.py:97]()

**Special handling for master:**
```python
if self.nnodes > 1 and self.dp_size == 1:
    if self.rank_in_node == 0:
        self.is_master_in_dp = True  # Node 0, rank 0 in node
    else:
        self.is_master_in_dp = False
```
[lightllm/server/router/model_infer/mode_backend/base_backend.py:809-818]()

### Request Processing Flow

```mermaid
graph TB
    Client["External Client"]
    
    subgraph "Node 0 (Master)"
        M_API["FastAPI Server<br/>:8000"]
        M_HTTP["HttpServerManager"]
        M_Router["RouterManager"]
        M_ShmBuffer["ShmObjsIOBuffer"]
        M_Model["Model RPC<br/>Processes 0..N-1"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Node 1..K (Workers)"
        W_ShmBuffer["ShmObjsIOBuffer"]
        W_Router["RouterManager"]
        W_Model["Model RPC<br/>Processes N..M"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Coordination"
        AllGather["NCCL all_gather_into_tensor"]
        Barrier["Synchronization Barriers"]
    end
    
    Client -->|"HTTP Request"| M_API
    M_API --> M_HTTP
    M_HTTP -->|"Write to SHM"| M_ShmBuffer
    M_ShmBuffer --> M_Router
    
    M_Router -->|"Check ready"| AllGather
    W_Router -->|"Check ready"| AllGather
    AllGather -->|"Synchronized"| M_Router
    AllGather -->|"Synchronized"| W_Router
    
    M_Router -->|"All nodes ready"| M_ShmBuffer
    W_Router -->|"All nodes ready"| W_ShmBuffer
    
    M_ShmBuffer -->|"Read reqs"| M_Model
    W_ShmBuffer -->|"Read reqs"| W_Model
    
    M_Model -->|"Forward pass"| Barrier
    W_Model -->|"Forward pass"| Barrier
    
    Barrier -->|"NCCL all-reduce"| M_Model
    Barrier -->|"NCCL all-reduce"| W_Model
    
    M_Model -->|"Results"| M_Router
    W_Model -->|"Results"| W_Router
    
    M_Router -->|"Response"| M_HTTP
    M_HTTP -->|"HTTP Response"| Client
    
    style M_API fill:#f9f9f9
    style AllGather fill:#f9f9f9
    style Barrier fill:#f9f9f9
```

### Synchronized Request Reading

All nodes must coordinate to read requests from shared memory simultaneously. This prevents race conditions and ensures consistency:

**Multi-Node TP Request Reading Logic:**
```python
def _try_read_new_reqs_multinode_tp(self):
    """
    Multi-node TP mode requires coordinating all rank behaviors synchronously.
    """
    # Each node checks if its shared memory buffer is ready
    if self.shm_reqs_io_buffer.is_ready():
        self.multinode_tp_gather_item_tensor.fill_(1)
    else:
        self.multinode_tp_gather_item_tensor.fill_(0)
    
    # All-gather to check if ALL nodes are ready
    dist.all_gather_into_tensor(
        self.multinode_tp_all_gather_tensor,
        self.multinode_tp_gather_item_tensor,
        group=self.multinode_tp_nccl_group,
        async_op=False,
    )
    
    # Only read if ALL nodes have ready buffers
    new_buffer_is_readys = self.multinode_tp_all_gather_tensor.detach().cpu().numpy()
    new_buffer_is_ready = np.all(new_buffer_is_readys == 1)
    
    if new_buffer_is_ready:
        self._read_reqs_buffer_and_init_reqs()
```
[lightllm/server/router/model_infer/mode_backend/base_backend.py:341-362]()

**Why synchronization is needed:**
- Master node writes requests to its shared memory
- Worker nodes need the same requests in their shared memory
- Without coordination, nodes may process different request sets
- `all_gather_into_tensor` ensures atomic "all ready" check

### Master-Only Operations

Certain operations only happen on the master node to avoid duplication:

**Writing shared memory state:**
```python
if is_master_in_dp:
    req.shm_req.shm_cur_kv_len = req.cur_kv_len
    req.shm_req.shm_cur_output_len = req.cur_output_len
    req.shm_req.finish_status = req.finish_status
```
[lightllm/server/router/model_infer/infer_batch.py:565-575]()

**Pausing requests:**
```python
if is_master_in_dp:
    req.shm_req.is_paused = True
```
[lightllm/server/router/model_infer/infer_batch.py:194-195]()

Sources: [lightllm/server/router/model_infer/mode_backend/base_backend.py:306-362](), [lightllm/server/router/model_infer/mode_backend/base_backend.py:797-824]()

## Rank and Node Identification

LightLLM maintains several rank identifiers for coordination in multi-node deployments:

### Rank Hierarchy

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Global Ranks (0 to tp-1)"
        GR["Global Process Group<br/>All processes across all nodes"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Node 0"
        N0R0["Rank 0<br/>global_rank=0<br/>rank_in_node=0"]
        N0R1["Rank 1<br/>global_rank=1<br/>rank_in_node=1"]
        N0RN["Rank N-1<br/>global_rank=N-1<br/>rank_in_node=N-1"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Node 1"
        N1R0["Rank N<br/>global_rank=N<br/>rank_in_node=0"]
        N1R1["Rank N+1<br/>global_rank=N+1<br/>rank_in_node=1"]
        N1RN["Rank 2N-1<br/>global_rank=2N-1<br/>rank_in_node=N-1"]
    end
    
    GR --> N0R0
    GR --> N0R1
    GR --> N0RN
    GR --> N1R0
    GR --> N1R1
    GR --> N1RN
    
    N0R0 -.->|"is_master_in_node"| N0R0
    N1R0 -.->|"is_master_in_node"| N1R0
    
    N0R0 -.->|"is_master_in_dp"| N0R0
```

### Rank Variables

**Initialization:**
```python
def init_rank_infos(self):
    self.node_world_size = get_node_world_size()  # GPUs per node
    self.rank_in_node = get_current_rank_in_node()  # 0 to node_world_size-1
    self.current_device_id = get_current_device_id()  # GPU device ID
    self.global_rank = get_global_rank()  # 0 to (nnodes * tp) - 1
    self.global_world_size = get_global_world_size()  # Total processes
    
    # Master determination
    if self.nnodes > 1 and self.dp_size == 1:
        # Multi-node TP: only rank 0 in node 0 is master
        if self.rank_in_node == 0:
            self.is_master_in_dp = True
        else:
            self.is_master_in_dp = False
    else:
        # Single node: rank 0 is master
        if self.rank_in_dp == 0:
            self.is_master_in_dp = True
        else:
            self.is_master_in_dp = False
    
    if self.rank_in_node == 0:
        self.is_master_in_node = True
    else:
        self.is_master_in_node = False
```
[lightllm/server/router/model_infer/mode_backend/base_backend.py:797-824]()

### Rank Usage Examples

| Variable | Usage |
|----------|-------|
| `global_rank` | PyTorch distributed operations (`dist.get_rank()`) |
| `rank_in_node` | CUDA device assignment, intra-node coordination |
| `is_master_in_node` | Node-local broadcast source |
| `is_master_in_dp` | Shared memory writes, request management |
| `node_world_size` | Number of GPUs per node |
| `global_world_size` | Total number of processes across all nodes |

**Example: Node-local broadcast**
```python
# Master rank in each node broadcasts readiness
src_rank_id = self.args.node_rank * self.node_world_size
dist.broadcast(
    self.node_broadcast_tensor, 
    src=src_rank_id, 
    group=self.node_nccl_group, 
    async_op=False
)
```
[lightllm/server/router/model_infer/mode_backend/base_backend.py:320-321]()

## Unique Server Naming

Each deployment instance (even on the same machine) requires a unique identifier for shared memory and other resources:

**Naming strategy:**
```python
def set_unique_server_name(args):
    if args.run_mode == "pd_master":
        os.environ["LIGHTLLM_UNIQUE_SERVICE_NAME_ID"] = str(args.port) + "_pd_master"
    else:
        os.environ["LIGHTLLM_UNIQUE_SERVICE_NAME_ID"] = str(args.nccl_port) + "_" + str(args.node_rank)
```
[lightllm/utils/envs_utils.py:12-17]()

**Purpose:**
- Prevents shared memory collisions between multiple deployments
- Each node gets unique SHM namespace
- Format: `{nccl_port}_{node_rank}` (e.g., "28765_0", "28765_1")

**Used for:**
- Shared memory segment names (`ShmReqManager`, `TokenLoad`, etc.)
- Shared arrays (`SharedInt`, `ReadOnlyStaticsMemoryManager`)
- Process naming (`setproctitle.setproctitle()`)

Sources: [lightllm/utils/envs_utils.py:12-17](), [lightllm/server/router/model_infer/mode_backend/base_backend.py:115]()

## Troubleshooting Multi-Node Setup

### Common Issues and Solutions

**1. NCCL Initialization Timeout**

**Symptoms:**
```
RuntimeError: NCCL initialization failed
```

**Causes and solutions:**
- **Firewall blocking:** Ensure `nccl_port` is open on all nodes
  ```bash
  sudo ufw allow 28765/tcp
  ```
- **Wrong nccl_host:** Worker nodes must use master node's IP
  ```bash
  # On worker nodes:
  --nccl_host 192.168.1.100  # Master node IP, not 127.0.0.1
  ```
- **Network interface:** Set NCCL to use correct interface
  ```bash
  export NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0  # Or your network interface
  ```

**2. Node IP Exchange Failure**

**Symptoms:**
- Nodes hang during startup
- `send_and_receive_node_ip()` timeout

**Solutions:**
- Verify `multinode_httpmanager_port` is accessible
- Check nodes can reach each other's HTTP coordination port:
  ```bash
  curl http://<other_node_ip>:12345
  ```
- Ensure all nodes start within a reasonable time window

**3. Request Processing Hangs**

**Symptoms:**
- Requests hang indefinitely
- No response from server

**Debug steps:**
1. Check NCCL debug output:
   ```bash
   export NCCL_DEBUG=INFO
   ```
2. Verify all model processes started successfully
3. Check for deadlocks in synchronization barriers
4. Inspect logs for NCCL errors or timeouts

**4. Port Conflicts**

**Symptoms:**
```
OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use
```

**Solutions:**
- Use different `nccl_port` for each deployment instance
- Ensure `multinode_httpmanager_port` and `multinode_router_gloo_port` are unique
- Check no other processes are using required ports:
  ```bash
  netstat -tuln | grep 28765
  ```

**5. Model Loading Imbalance**

**Symptoms:**
- Some nodes finish loading quickly, others timeout
- `dist.barrier()` hangs

**Solutions:**
- Ensure all nodes have same model files locally
- Check disk I/O speed on all nodes
- Verify identical `model_dir` path on all nodes
- Use shared filesystem (NFS) with good performance

**6. Asymmetric Network Performance**

**Symptoms:**
- Slow inference despite multi-node setup
- High latency between nodes

**Debug:**
```bash
# Test network bandwidth between nodes
iperf3 -s  # On one node
iperf3 -c <node_ip>  # On another node

# Test NCCL bandwidth
python -m torch.distributed.launch \
    --nproc_per_node=1 \
    --nnodes=2 \
    --node_rank=0 \
    nccl_bench.py
```

**Solutions:**
- Use InfiniBand or 100GbE networking
- Ensure low-latency interconnect between nodes
- Check for network congestion
- Consider P-D separation if latency is high

Sources: [lightllm/server/api_start.py:95-97](), [lightllm/server/router/model_infer/mode_backend/base_backend.py:341-362]()

## Advanced Configuration

### Config Server for Multiple Deployments

When running multiple independent LightLLM deployments, use config server mode to manage NCCL initialization:

**Start config server:**
```bash
python -m lightllm.server.api_server \
    --run_mode config_server \
    --config_server_host 192.168.1.50 \
    --config_server_port 29000
```

**Start deployments with config server:**
```bash
# Deployment 1 - Node 0
python -m lightllm.server.api_server \
    --model_dir /model1 \
    --tp 8 --nnodes 2 --node_rank 0 \
    --nccl_host 192.168.1.50 \
    --nccl_port 28000 \
    --use_config_server_to_init_nccl \
    --config_server_host 192.168.1.50 \
    --config_server_port 29000

# Deployment 2 - Node 0 (different nccl_port)
python -m lightllm.server.api_server \
    --model_dir /model2 \
    --tp 8 --nnodes 2 --node_rank 0 \
    --nccl_host 192.168.1.50 \
    --nccl_port 28100 \
    --use_config_server_to_init_nccl \
    --config_server_host 192.168.1.50 \
    --config_server_port 29000
```

**Requirements:**
- `nccl_host` must equal `config_server_host`
- Each deployment must use unique `nccl_port`
- Config server acts as centralized TCP store

Sources: [lightllm/server/api_cli.py:195-200](), [lightllm/server/api_start.py:95-98]()

### Health Monitoring in Multi-Node Setup

Each node runs health monitoring independently, but only the master node exposes the HTTP health endpoint:

**Health check behavior:**
```python
async def health_check(args, httpserver_manager, request):
    # Adjust expected tokens for prefill-only nodes
    if args.run_mode in ["prefill", "nixl_prefill"]:
        request_dict["parameters"]["max_new_tokens"] = 1
```
[lightllm/utils/health_check.py:70-74]()

**Monitoring setup:**
- Master node: Full health check via HTTP API
- Worker nodes: Internal process monitoring only
- Health monitor process checks all local processes
- Failure threshold: 3 consecutive failures by default

## Performance Considerations

### Network Bandwidth Requirements

**Minimum recommendations:**
- **InfiniBand:** HDR (200 Gbps) or better for optimal performance
- **Ethernet:** 100GbE minimum, 200GbE+ recommended
- **Latency:** <10μs preferred for InfiniBand, <50μs for Ethernet

**Bandwidth calculation:**
```
Per-layer all-reduce size (bytes) ≈ hidden_size * hidden_size * 2 (fp16)
Total communication per forward pass ≈ num_layers * all-reduce size
```

For 70B model (hidden_size=8192, 80 layers):
- Per-layer: 8192 * 8192 * 2 = 134 MB
- Total: ~10.7 GB per forward pass
- With 8 tokens/sec throughput: ~86 Gbps required

### Load Balancing

Multi-node TP distributes computation evenly, but consider:

**GPU utilization:**
- All GPUs should have similar memory and compute capacity
- Mixed GPU types (e.g., A100 + H100) will bottleneck at slower GPU
- Monitor GPU utilization across all nodes

**Model weight distribution:**
- Weights are sharded evenly across all GPUs
- Each node loads `1/nnodes` of the model
- Ensure all nodes have identical storage performance

**Request distribution:**
- Master node receives all requests
- Computation is distributed via tensor parallelism
- Consider data parallelism if master node becomes bottleneck

Sources: [lightllm/server/router/model_infer/mode_backend/base_backend.py:75-228]()

This document provides practical guidance for deploying LightLLM in different environments and scenarios. It covers installation methods, deployment mode selection, and common configuration patterns. For detailed architectural information about distributed modes, see [Distributed Architecture](#7). For API configurations, see [API Reference](#6).

## Overview

LightLLM can be deployed in several ways to accommodate different infrastructure and performance requirements:

1. **Installation Method**:
   - Python package (`pip install lightllm`)
   - Docker container (`ghcr.io/modeltc/lightllm:main`)

2. **Deployment Scale**:
   - Single-node (covered in [Standard Single-Node Deployment](#8.2))
   - Multi-node distributed (covered in [Multi-Node Setup](#7.6))

3. **Operational Mode**:
   - Normal mode (all-in-one process)
   - P-D separation mode (specialized prefill/decode nodes, detailed in [Prefill-Decode Separation](#7.4))

This page provides an overview of deployment approaches. For detailed information, see:
- [Docker Deployment](#8.1) - Using official Docker images
- [Standard Single-Node Deployment](#8.2) - Running on a single machine
- [Production Deployment Best Practices](#8.3) - Production-grade configurations

## Installation Methods

### Python Package Installation

LightLLM can be installed as a Python package with its dependencies managed through `setup.py` and `requirements.txt`.

**Installation Steps**:

```bash
# Install from PyPI
pip install lightllm

# Or install from source
git clone https://github.com/ModelTC/lightllm.git
cd lightllm
pip install -e .
```

**Key Dependencies** (from requirements.txt):
- `torch==2.8.0` - PyTorch framework
- `transformers==4.53.3` - HuggingFace transformers
- `fastapi==0.115.6` - HTTP API server
- `gunicorn==23.0.0` - WSGI HTTP server
- `triton` - Custom CUDA kernel support
- `flashinfer-python==0.2.4` - FlashInfer attention kernels
- `pyzmq==25.1.1b2` - ZeroMQ for inter-process communication
- `rpyc==5.3.1` - RPC framework

**Launch Command**:

```bash
python -m lightllm.server.api_server \
    --model_dir /path/to/model \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8000 \
    --tp 1
```

### Docker Container Installation

LightLLM provides official Docker images built via GitHub Actions and published to GitHub Container Registry.

**Available Images**:
- `ghcr.io/modeltc/lightllm:main` - Latest build from main branch
- `ghcr.io/modeltc/lightllm:main-deepep` - Specialized build for DeepSeek models
- `ghcr.io/modeltc/lightllm:v*.*.*` - Tagged releases

**Quick Launch Script**:

LightLLM includes a convenience script `tools/quick_launch_docker.py` for simplified Docker deployment:

```bash
python tools/quick_launch_docker.py \
    --model /path/to/model \
    --port 8080 \
    --num-proc 4 \
    --max-total-tokens 8192
```

**Script Parameters**:
| Parameter | Description | Default |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| `--image` | Docker image to use | `ghcr.io/modeltc/lightllm:main` |
| `--name` | Container name | (auto-generated) |
| `--shm-size` | Shared memory size | Half of RAM |
| `--model` | Model directory path | (required) |
| `--port` | Service port | `8080` |
| `--num-proc` | Number of GPUs/processes | `1` |
| `--max-total-tokens` | Max token capacity | `4096` |

**Manual Docker Launch**:

```bash
docker run -it --gpus all \
    -p 8000:8000 \
    -v /path/to/model:/models \
    --shm-size 10g \
    ghcr.io/modeltc/lightllm:main \
    python -m lightllm.server.api_server \
    --model_dir /models \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8000 \
    --tp 4
```

## Choosing a Deployment Mode

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Start["Start Deployment Planning"]
    
    Start --> Q1{"Single machine<br/>or multiple machines?"}
    
    Q1 -->|"Single machine"| Q2{"Need multimodal<br/>(vision/audio)?"}
    Q1 -->|"Multiple machines"| MultiNode["Multi-Node Setup<br/>See section 7.6"]
    
    Q2 -->|"No"| Q3{"GPU memory<br/>sufficient?"}
    Q2 -->|"Yes"| Multimodal["Enable Multimodal<br/>--enable_multimodal<br/>--enable_multimodal_audio"]
    
    Q3 -->|"Yes"| Normal["Normal Mode<br/>--run_mode=normal<br/>See section 8.2"]
    Q3 -->|"No"| Q4{"Can add more GPUs?"}
    
    Q4 -->|"Yes"| TP["Increase Tensor Parallel<br/>--tp N"]
    Q4 -->|"No"| Quant["Enable Quantization<br/>--mode triton_int8kv<br/>See section 4.5"]
    
    Multimodal --> Normal
    TP --> Normal
    Quant --> Normal
    
    Q1 -->|"Need high throughput"| Q5{"Separate prefill<br/>and decode?"}
    
    Q5 -->|"Yes"| PDMode["P-D Separation<br/>--run_mode=pd_master/prefill/decode<br/>See section 7.4"]
    Q5 -->|"No"| Normal
    
    style Normal fill:#e1f5ff
    style PDMode fill:#ffe1e1
    style MultiNode fill:#e1ffe1
    style Multimodal fill:#fff4e1
```

**Decision Criteria**:

1. **Normal Mode** (`--run_mode=normal`):
   - Single-node deployment
   - Model fits on available GPUs with tensor parallelism
   - Simplest setup, recommended for most use cases
   - Covered in detail in [Standard Single-Node Deployment](#8.2)

2. **P-D Separation Mode**:
   - High-throughput scenarios requiring specialized compute
   - Separate prefill (compute-intensive) and decode (memory-intensive) workloads
   - Requires multiple nodes or node groups
   - Detailed in [Prefill-Decode Separation](#7.4)

3. **Multi-Node Mode**:
   - Model too large for single-node tensor parallelism
   - Requires distributed NCCL communication
   - Detailed in [Multi-Node Setup](#7.6)

Sources: [lightllm/server/api_cli.py:7-16](), [lightllm/server/api_start.py:63-79]()

## Common Configuration Parameters

LightLLM deployment is configured through command-line arguments defined in `api_cli.py` via the `make_argument_parser()` function. Below are the most commonly used parameters grouped by category.

### Essential Parameters

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| `--host` | Server host address | `127.0.0.1` |
| `--port` | HTTP server port | `8000` |
| `--model_dir` | Model weight directory path | (required) |
| `--run_mode` | Deployment mode | `normal` |

### Resource Configuration

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| `--tp` | Tensor parallelism size | `1` |
| `--dp` | Data parallelism size (DeepSeek models) | `1` |
| `--max_total_token_num` | Maximum total tokens | Auto-calculated |
| `--mem_fraction` | GPU memory usage ratio | `0.9` |
| `--batch_max_tokens` | Max tokens per batch | Auto-calculated |

### Performance Tuning

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| `--disable_cudagraph` | Disable CUDA graphs | `False` |
| `--chunked_prefill_size` | Chunked prefill size | `4096` |
| `--router_max_wait_tokens` | Schedule interval | `1` |
| `--enable_flashinfer_prefill` | Use FlashInfer for prefill | `False` |
| `--enable_flashinfer_decode` | Use FlashInfer for decode | `False` |
| `--enable_fa3` | Use FlashAttention 3 | `False` |

### Multimodal Support

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| `--enable_multimodal` | Enable vision models | `False` |
| `--enable_multimodal_audio` | Enable audio models | `False` |
| `--visual_gpu_ids` | GPU IDs for visual models | `[0]` |
| `--visual_tp` | Visual model tensor parallel | `1` |
| `--visual_dp` | Visual model data parallel | `1` |

### Quantization

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| `--mode` | Model mode (e.g., `triton_int8kv`) | `[]` |
| `--quant_type` | Weight quantization method | `none` |
| `--data_type` | Model data type | Auto-detected |

**Example: Basic Single-GPU Deployment**

```bash
python -m lightllm.server.api_server \

    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8000
```

**Example: Multi-GPU with Optimizations**

```bash
python -m lightllm.server.api_server \

    --port 8000 \
```
